checks: GitHub CI on the PR (real Prisma engines, from-scratch migrations): ALL GREEN. That covers lint, typecheck, migrations, the hand-written invariant asserts, the drift check, the unit suite under both TZs, the production build and the full e2e on the production build (port 3400). Locally: lint ok; typecheck ok. vitest: TZ=UTC 1144 pass / 13 fail; TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati 1142 pass / 15 fail. All failures are in loyalty/placement/remake/rush/snapshot DB tests, which also fail on main (16 there). Environment limit: binaries.prisma.sh is blocked, so the client was generated locally (uncommitted, reverted) with engineType=client + @prisma/adapter-pg, and P2002 meta, enum introspection and concurrency behave differently under it. next build --webpack ok; the Turbopack build is blocked locally (fonts.googleapis.com unreachable; fonts mocked). Playwright e2e on that production build: 240 pass / 15 skipped / 14 fail. 13 of the failures are specs that run db:rush:test, which hits the same (businessDay, seq) adapter limit as the unit rush.test on main. The 14th is brand.spec asserting the font, which was mocked. auth/checkout/loyalty/status/kitchen specs pass. Manual: curl showed the headers; the bad-env boot is refused by name. Migration applied by hand to local PG16. Prisma drift check not run locally (no schema engine); PR CI runs it.

K1.text: Staff cookie is still a salted but deterministic SHA-256 digest of the shared passcode. There are no session rows, and the only revocation is rotating the passcode for everyone (SEC-03). There are no sign-in links. Checked by reading staff-auth.ts, login/actions.ts and middleware.ts.
K1.gap_reason: Shared passcode by design: candidate for 'accepted' (GAP-PLAN step 1), which needs an owner decision-log row. Otherwise it needs a new session system, which is out of scope here.

K2.text: Single shared passcode with no second factor and no per-user roles. Checked by reading login/actions.ts.
K2.gap_reason: Accepted candidate (shared passcode by design). Needs an owner decision-log row, or a new MFA system, which is not built here.

K3.text: On the branch, every kitchen page (8) calls requireStaffPage, both kitchen route handlers (events, report/export) return staffRouteRefusal first, and every 'use server' export in app/kitchen (except login) calls requireStaff() first: 44 exports in 4 files. All use the same staffCookieGeneration as the middleware. Checked with a full sweep of 7 'use server' files, 18 pages and 3 route handlers. cart, checkout, /api/updates and /status are public by design. require-staff.test.ts scans the source and fails on a missing guard (verified by removing one). The e2e auth.spec passes.
K3.evidence: apps/web/lib/require-staff.ts; apps/web/lib/require-staff.test.ts; apps/web/app/kitchen/actions.ts; apps/web/app/kitchen/menu/actions.ts; apps/web/app/kitchen/settings/actions.ts; apps/web/app/kitchen/loyalty/actions.ts; apps/web/app/kitchen/events/route.ts; apps/web/app/kitchen/report/export/route.ts
K3.change: 5457e25: requireStaff/requireStaffPage/staffRouteRefusal at every kitchen entry point, plus the source-scan test

K4.text: Single-restaurant, single-tenant product with no customer accounts. Kitchen by-id reads are staff-only and global by design. The customer status handle is the 192-bit token itself, and a wrong token gets notFound. Spot check.

K5.text: On the branch, a Postgres RateLimit table holds fixed-window counters, one atomic upsert per hit. Limits apply to kitchen sign-in (10/15m per IP), verification start (10 per IP, 5 per hashed phone), verification confirm (20 per IP), placement (120 per IP) and status-token reads (300 per IP). The retention sweep cleans up old windows. On main there was no limiter anywhere (grepped). The DB test passes, including a race of 10 concurrent hits with exactly 3 admitted.
K5.evidence: packages/db/rate-limit.ts; packages/db/rate-limit.test.ts; packages/db/prisma/migrations/20261113100000_rate_limit/migration.sql; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts; apps/web/app/kitchen/login/actions.ts; apps/web/app/checkout/actions.ts; apps/web/app/status/[token]/page.tsx
K5.change: 8390aa2: RateLimit model + migration, limiter, call sites, sweep

K6.text: On the branch, /status/:path* sends no-referrer, X-Robots-Tag noindex and Cache-Control private, no-store. Verified by a unit test and by curl against next start. The status token is still stored raw (unique column) with no expiry or revocation.
K6.gap_reason: Hashing at rest changes a contract: the idempotent placement replay (findUnique by idempotencyKey) returns statusToken from the row. Expiry and revocation change what customers see. Both need an owner design decision (SEC-05).

K7.text: On the branch, next.config.ts headers() sends Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, nosniff, CSP frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options DENY and HSTS (2y, includeSubDomains) on /:path*. poweredByHeader is off. Verified by a unit test and by curl against a production build.

K8.text: Passcode compare is constant-time over fixed-length digests. An unset STAFF_PASSCODE locks /kitchen. An unset pepper refuses enrolment and token minting. PIN, code and verified-token checks use timingSafeEqual. No NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_ vars, no tracked .env except .env.example (names only), and no secrets in query strings. Checked with a grep plus a read of the auth and verification files.

K9.text: No inbound webhooks: the only route handlers are /api/updates, /kitchen/events and /kitchen/report/export, and payment is a mock provider. Full listing of route.ts files.

K10.text: stubSmsVerifyProvider returns the code, and requestCheckoutVerification sends echoedCode to the browser. That includes production builds, and nothing fails loudly. The structured logs (placement/export lines) carry no tokens or bodies.
K10.gap_reason: Making production refuse the stub would break self-serve reward redemption on the live demo, which changes behaviour users see. Gating it needs a new env value. Both need an owner decision, or a real SMS provider (SEC-01, GAP-PLAN step 4).

K11.text: On the branch, apps/web/lib/env.ts validates DATABASE_URL (required, postgres/prisma URL), DIRECT_URL, PORT and NODE_ENV, and fails with names only. instrumentation.ts runs it once at server start. Verified on next start: a bad DATABASE_URL makes requests fail with 'Invalid environment: DATABASE_URL'. .env.example names every process.env read in apps/packages/scripts, with tooling vars commented, and env.test.ts enforces that.
K11.change: b7462ca: env schema at boot + .env.example completeness test

K12.text: Tests run on local Postgres (.env.test first-wins). resetDatabase(), used by every DB test, the seed and the rush, calls assertLocalDatabase, which refuses non-local hosts. e2e runs build:test then start:test (a production build).
